title: Google Playground ile kod yazmadan yapay zeka ile oyun geliştirilebilecek
summary: Google, kullanıcıların tek satır kod yazmadan sadece fikirlerini yazarak tarayıcı üzerinden oyun oluşturmasını sağlayan Playground adlı yapay zeka deneyimini duyurdu.
body:
Android Authority'nin aktardığına göre Google, kullanıcıların hiçbir kodlama bilgisi olmadan yapay zeka aracılığıyla oyun tasarlamasını sağlayan yeni deneysel platformu **Google Playground**'u kullanıma sundu. Tarayıcı üzerinden çalışan bu platform, kullanıcıların metin komutlarıyla 2D veya 3D oyunlar oluşturmasına, karakterleri ve kuralları değiştirmesine imkan tanıyor. 

## Google Playground nasıl çalışıyor?

Sohbet tabanlı bir arayüze sahip olan platformda, sıfırdan bir fikir yazabilir, mevcut şablonları düzenleyebilir ya da rehberli destek alarak oyun konseptinizi şekillendirebilirsiniz. Oluşturulan oyunlar arkadaşlarınızla paylaşılabiliyor veya galeriye yüklenebiliyor. Seçilen oyun türlerinde ise çok oyunculu modlar ve liderlik tabloları destekleniyor. Alt yapı olarak Google'ın temel modellerini kullanan sistem, ABD'deki 18 yaş ve üzerindeki kullanıcılara sunulurken, içerik oluşturma erişimi Google One üyeliğine göre kademeli olarak açılıyor.

## Unity Spark entegrasyonu yolda

Google ve Unity ayrıca gelecekteki bir güncellemeyle platforma Unity Spark entegrasyonunun ekleneceğini duyurdu. Bu entegrasyon sayesinde profesyonel düzeyde mekanikler ve gelişmiş üç boyutlu yetenekler sisteme dahil olacak. Kapalı beta süreci için bekleme listesi başlarken, bu araçla yapılan oyunlar da platform üzerinden paylaşılabilecek.

**Neden önemli?** Google Playground, oyun geliştirme sürecindeki teknik engelleri ortadan kaldırarak genel kullanıcıların yapay zeka yardımıyla doğrudan tarayıcı üzerinden kendi oyunlarını üretmesine ve paylaşmasına olanak tanıyor.

source_texts.text:
Google's latest experiment lets you build games with just an idea, no code
Oct 7, 2026 — 8:00 AM ET
- Google has launched a new AI experiment called “Playground.”
- It lets users create games without writing a single line of code. Playground games support leaderboards, multiplayer, and sharing with friends.
- Playground is available in the US to users aged 18 or above.
If you enjoy playing games on your phone or PC, you’ve probably had several ideas for the kind of game you’d like to develop if you had the skills and technical know-how. While there’s a certain sense of accomplishment in learning game development, 3D modeling, character rigging, etc., and applying them to build your own game, Google wants to use AI to make the process much, much easier.
Google today launched Playground, a new AI experiment that lets users bring their game ideas to life using natural language prompts. Just describe a game idea, art style, and mechanics, and Playground can turn it into a playable demo.
Users can iterate on their ideas, make changes, and improve or adjust anything in the game. Google Playground also offers several starter prompts that users can remix to create new games, along with guided support to help shape game concepts.
Once created, users can play the game, share it with friends, or publish it to the Playground gallery. They can also play games created by other users, with support for in-game leaderboards and multiplayer gaming for select game genres. Since Playground games are all browser-based games, users can play them on their phones or laptops.
The Playground app connects with your Play Games account, so you can like your favorite games, join leaderboards, and follow creators to stay updated on their latest launches.
Google has also announced that the Playground app will add support for Unity Spark integration in a future update. Once this integration is live, users will be able to use Unity Spark’s advanced mechanics and 3D capabilities to create even more immersive games with natural language prompts.
Playground is currently only available in the US to users aged 18 or older. All eligible users can access the Playground experiment from its website and play games. Creation access is rolling out in tiers based on users’ Google One membership.

source_texts.text:
Google today announced Playground, a new browser-based platform for making custom games from AI prompts. Playground will be available today in the US for users who are 18 and older at playground.google.
Google now lets you make games with AI
Google Playground is a browser-based tool for making games from AI prompts.
The company is pitching it as an “experimental gaming platform” that “lowers the barriers to creation” and doesn’t require coding experience. “With Playground’s conversational interface, you can direct the game just by typing what you want to build,” Google says in a blog post. “Start from a blank canvas, remix starter prompts, or use guided support to shape your concept — and then test it right away. Want to tweak the physics, rewrite the rules, customize the characters, or overhaul the environment? Just ask. You stay in complete control of the creative direction from rough concept to final polish.”
When you’re finished making your game, you can share it with a link or publish it to the “Playground Explore gallery” so others can play it. “Select genres” will support in-game leaderboards and multiplayer. The gallery will highlight games that are “fresh, creative, and fun” using ratings and play activity, according to Google.
Playground is free to use, but if you have a Google One subscription, you’ll have higher weekly token limits based on your plan, Google spokesperson Nia Carter tells The Verge. Under the hood, Playground is powered by “Google’s existing foundation models (Gemini, Nano Banana, and Lyria) paired with a custom harness refined through our own internally built games and evaluations,” Carter says.
Alongside today’s Playground announcement, Google and Unity are also revealing Unity Spark, an AI game-making experience that’s closer to a professional-level game development engine and allows you to create games simultaneously with others. Games made with Unity Spark will be shareable on Playground. A closed beta for Spark is scheduled to kick off later this year, and people who are interested can get on a waitlist starting today.
Google’s news today follows Meta’s recent announcement that it will let users build games with AI on their phones and on the web for its Horizon platform with new apps rolling out in early access. Published games made with those tools will be able to be recommended on Facebook and Instagram, which could give them more reach than they would have just being on Horizon. Roblox has also started letting users make games with AI on their phones as part of a “Build” feature that’s in public alpha testing in a few countries.

source_texts.text:
Google's experimental Playground platform uses AI to create games for you
It will design games based on your prompts.
Google has launched a new AI-powered experimental gaming platform called Playground, which lets you create games without needing to know how to code or draw. It has an interface similar to most AI chatbots, where you can type in a prompt for the kind of game you want to build. You can also choose whether to create a 2D or 3D game and, for select genres, whether it's single-player or multiplayer.
While you can write your prompt from scratch, you can also remix some starter prompts or use guided support. After the initial output, you can shape the game mechanics, physics and graphics with further prompts. For example, if you're making a platformer, you can tell Playground to let the player double-jump so they can reach higher platforms a single jump can't reach.
Of course, a platform like Playground that lowers the barrier to game creation could lead to low-quality titles. But it doesn't sound like you have to worry about them flooding Google Play — for now, anyway. If you want to share your game, you can either drop a shareable link to friends or publish it to the Playground Explore gallery that the community can enjoy. You can also keep your game private. Games you publish will support in-game leaderboards.
Playground will soon offer Unity Spark integration, as well. Google says Spark "unlocks robust, professional-level mechanics, high-fidelity 3D capabilities and the flexibility of the Unity runtime" to help you create better, higher-level games. And since Playground is still experimental, the company expects to roll out more changes in the future. The platform is now available on the official Playground website if you're in the US and 18 or older. However, access will be tiered based on your Google One membership.
